response.title: which power station makes the least fan noise when running a fridge at night
response.answer:
For running a refrigerator at night, I'd prioritize a portable power station with fanless operation at low loads, rather than one advertised as having a quiet fan.

A typical household refrigerator draws around 50–200W while its compressor is running, although startup power can be much higher. At those loads, some power stations can operate without turning on their cooling fans.

The important distinction is:

Silent at 100W: Ideal for a refrigerator during normal operation.

Quiet at 300–500W: Useful, but doesn't guarantee the fan won't cycle overnight.

Quiet charging mode: Not particularly relevant if you're using the station on battery power overnight.

My top picks for quiet overnight refrigerator use

Anker claims approximately 20 dB below 200W. A particularly promising choice for a fridge drawing 100–150W, though zero fan cycling isn't guaranteed.

EcoFlow claims below 30 dB at loads up to 600W. One independent comparison measured 41 dB in its noise test, but that isn't a fridge-specific measurement.

BLUETTI 1800W LFP Battery Generator,1024Wh Portable Power St…

1,024Wh · 1,800W AC

$498.99

Advertised around 30 dB below 600W. Another strong candidate, although I haven't found enough comparable fridge-load fan measurements to rank it ahead of Anker. 
The Power Station Guide

My provisional winner is the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 for a conventional fridge drawing under 200W. However, the published ratings use different test conditions, so none establishes which unit has the fewest fan starts during an entire night.

For runtime, a 1,024Wh power station might last roughly 8–16 hours with a fridge averaging 50–100W, depending on inverter losses and compressor cycling.
